The Commission issued Order proposing “Determination of levellised generic tariff for FY 2018-19 under Regulation 8 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions for Tariff determination from Renewable Energy Sources) Regulations, 2017”, (Petition No. 02/SM/2018) dated 1 st March 2018 and invited comments/suggestions/objections from the stakeholders. A Public Notice was also issued on 1 st March 2018 stating the last date of submission of comments/suggestions/objections as 21 st March 2018. 5. In response, written comments/suggestions/objections were received from only one stakeholder, i.e The South Indian Sugar Mills Association (SISMA) 6. Subsequently, a public hearing was held on 26 th March 2018, following which submission was made by Rajasthan SLDC. 7. The Commission has considered the views/comments/suggestions of the stakeholders and the analysis/decisions of the Commission thereon is presented as under: Rs. 1834.89/MT to Rs. 2910/MT. They have strongly objected to Commission’s proposal of Bagasse prices for Tamil Nadu as Rs. 1834.89/MT. They have highlighted that last year too, for Draft RE Tariff Regulations 2017, they had furnished detailed justification as well as documentary support and strongly pleaded that the Draft Regulations should determine bagasse price for Tamil Nadu not below Rs. 2300/MT for FY 2017-18. However, in the final regulations there was no change. Hence, SISMA filed a writ petition No.23193/2017 before Madras High Court specifically challenging clause No 49 in CERC Regulations 2017 which states that bagasse price for cogeneration plants in Tamil Nadu would be Rs.1,747.51/ton for FY 2017-18. Further, they have cited that TNERC vide their public notice dated 02.03.2018 has put on public domain, a consultative paper for determining tariff for bagasse based cogeneration plants in Tamil Nadu for the control period 2018-20. In the said consultative paper, TNERC has considered bagasse price as Rs.1,834.89/ton based on CERC Regulations 2017 resulting in low tariff for Bagasse based projects. SISMA has further highlighted that Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited( TNPL) a Government of Tamil Nadu undertaking buys bagasse regularly from sugar mills in the State and pays a price in excess of Rs.2,300/ton last year . Accordingly, they have requested to make this as a basis for determining market price for bagasse. Further, a writ petition has been filed before the Madras High Court challenging clause No 49 in CERC RE Tariff Regulations, 2017 which provides for the bagasse price for cogeneration plants. The matter is subjudice in the Court. Hence, the Commission has decided to retain the proposed fuel prices for Bagasse based cogeneration plants for the purpose of tariff determination. The Commission would like to clarify that the request of Rajasthan SLDC for exemption from levy of GST on Renewable Energy projects is beyond the scope of the jurisdiction of this Commission. 8. No other comment on any other parameters of the order was received.
